articles.title: Share a song without choosing someone else’s music service
articles.dek: The beta Share Links plugin covers tracks, albums and artists, with a preview before sending.
body: A recommendation can open through the recipient’s own Music Assistant instance or a public music-service link. Share appears beside tracks, albums and artists, in track queues and in the full-screen player.

The dialog shows the item and its service links before it is shared. The link carries identifying information and public artwork addresses, rather than audio files, and does not grant access to the sender’s server.
The server’s Share Links plugin and a separate landing page connect those choices. Playlist sharing and importing a shared playlist are outside this addition.

articles.title: Camera cards out of view stop keeping a processor busy
articles.dek: The problem was especially visible in the Mac companion app, whose dashboard can remain active in the background.
body: Loading indicators for cameras below the visible part of a dashboard could keep redrawing the page even though no snapshot had been requested. On one Mac with six off-screen cameras, the app’s web-content process used 97–99% of a processor core; pausing those animations reduced it to about 2%.

Home Assistant only creates the indicator when the camera card comes into view. In the same dashboard test, the corrected version had no running off-screen animations, while scrolling to the cameras still loaded and refreshed their pictures.
Misha Hawthorn makes a first contribution to the frontend with the correction.

articles.title: Send another Android app’s sound to your speakers
articles.dek: Android 10 or later can capture permitted media audio, with an explicit recording prompt.
body: Audio from another app can become a source for a compatible Music Assistant player. The Android app asks permission to capture playback and sends the sound to the selected speaker; stopping that player or the capture notification ends the session.

This uses Android’s playback-capture facility, which requires Android 10 or later. Apps can disallow capture, and the feature does not promise to forward phone calls or every sound on the device. The local phone player is excluded as a destination to avoid feeding its own sound back into itself.

articles.title: Keep your phone’s history when a cloud link breaks
articles.dek: Android tries the remaining server addresses before replacing a registration, and local notifications reconnect when its identity changes.
body: A saved cloud address that returned “not found” could make the app register the same phone again on every start, even when a local server address still worked. That left duplicate devices and disrupted their history, while local push notifications stayed attached to the old registration.

Timothy makes the Android app try its other server addresses before deciding the registration is broken. If registration really changes, the notification connection follows the new identity on its next check, within 30 seconds, rather than waiting for an app restart.

pullRequests.title: Improve re-registration when answer is 404

articles.title: Sleep longer between Thread check-ins without losing the connection
articles.dek: Makers gain longer intervals, but existing settings above two hours need changing.
body: A sleepy Thread device can lose its parent connection—the nearby device that relays its messages—when more than three minutes pass between checks. ESPHome adjusts the connection timeouts to the chosen interval so the device can check less often without being treated as disconnected.

Configurations using device_type: MTD need poll_period set to two hours or less. Larger values are limited to two hours with a warning and become validation errors in ESPHome 2027.6.0. Intervals supplied by custom code have the same limit.

The three advanced core_options for the child timeout and supervision timers must use whole numbers of seconds: write 240 instead of an expression such as (4 * 60). Explicitly disabled supervision stays disabled.

articles.title: Plan around pollen and weather warnings in Belgium
articles.dek: Warnings follow the selected location and language; a failed pollen lookup leaves ordinary forecasts working.
body: Seven pollen types receive their own translated readings in Home Assistant’s IRM KMI integration. Each shows the level published by the Belgian weather service, giving automations a separate signal for each type.

A warning signal turns on while an alert applies to the chosen location, and another reading gives the next warning’s start time. The full list distinguishes active warnings from those published ahead of time.

articles.title: Choose a floor, then leave out a room
articles.dek: Status choices form clearer pairs, and disabled entities appear among unavailable results.
body: Unticking one room after selecting its floor keeps the other rooms selected. The floor changes to a partly selected state, then becomes fully selected again when the last room is restored. This applies across Home Assistant’s device, automation, script, scene and helper lists.

On the entities page, paired choices such as Available and Unavailable sit together beneath a named heading. Selecting a pair selects both choices, while a partial selection stays visible. Disabled entities also appear under Unavailable instead of falling outside both availability choices.
Lex Postma makes a first contribution to the frontend with the changes, developed at the Open Home Hackathon in The Hague.

articles.title: Emby books keep their place across listening apps
articles.dek: Multi-file titles appear as one item, with a chapter for each file.
body: Audiobook libraries stored in Emby join the searchable and browsable Music Assistant library. Several files belonging to one book play as a single item rather than a loose collection of tracks.

Listening progress is read from and written back to the Emby account, so the saved position can follow the listener between the two services. The connection specifically recognizes Emby libraries configured as audiobooks.

articles.title: Most Cast speakers switch to MP3 by default
articles.dek: Lossless audio remains an option; Chromecast Audio, Nest Hub and explicit format choices keep their settings.
body: Long radio sessions or continuous queues could fall silent on some Nest and Samsung Cast speakers using lossless FLAC audio. Music Assistant changes the default to compressed MP3 for most receivers; owners can still select FLAC themselves.

On a Samsung Music Frame, the investigation recorded three failures during about eight and a half hours of lossless playback. MP3 and AAC ran for almost seven hours without the same failure. Chromecast Audio and Nest Hub retain their FLAC default after passing the longer tests.

A companion change detects a speaker that drops its stream while still reporting playback. After fifteen seconds without a new request, it can restart from the track’s position or rejoin a live source, while leaving deliberate pauses, stops and takeovers alone.

articles.title: Fresh installations get a 15-minute setup window
articles.dek: Restarting reopens initial account creation; an authenticated Home Assistant administrator can use the panel at any time.
body: An unclaimed server should not leave its first administrator account open for someone to claim indefinitely. The public setup page accepts that first account only during the first 15 minutes after Music Assistant starts.

After the deadline, the page asks for a restart to try again. Setup through the Home Assistant panel remains available to an authenticated administrator, and creating any administrator closes public setup permanently, including across restarts.

articles.title: Homemade Zigbee devices report their own battery
articles.dek: ZHA receives both level and voltage; Zigbee2MQTT needs a custom converter for the voltage reading.
body: A battery-powered ESP32 device can expose its remaining charge through Zigbee’s standard battery reporting rather than as a generic sensor. ESPHome connects its battery-level and voltage sensors to the device’s power information, with documentation showing the configuration.

ZHA exposes voltage as an extra attribute of the battery entity. Zigbee2MQTT automatically detects the battery level, while a separate voltage entity needs a custom converter. These readings describe the device’s own battery, not an external battery being monitored.

articles.title: Spelled-out numbers stop tripping up voice commands
articles.dek: Swiss German spellings gain a match, while Russian timer replies handle words as well as digits.
body: A transcription such as “dreissig” should mean thirty just as “dreißig” does. Hassil, the sentence matcher used by Assist, adds the spelling used in Switzerland to its German number lists, covering requests such as brightness, volume, temperature and timer duration.

Russian timer responses receive a separate correction for numbers written as words. Starting, extending or shortening a timer no longer tries to treat those words as digits when composing the reply, and the response chooses the appropriate form of “minute”, “hour” or “second”.
Ahmet Selim Fedakar makes a first contribution to Hassil with the German correction; @ikarkharkov makes a first contribution to the intents repository with the Russian timer work.

articles.title: A better route for pairing battery-free devices
articles.dek: Bidirectional Green Power devices also keep reporting when an old setup message arrives late.
body: When several Zigbee relays heard the same setup request, choosing the first could leave a battery-free Green Power device without a reply. Zigpy, the library behind ZHA’s Zigbee communication, considers the nearby relays together and selects a suitable one with the strongest link.

A late copy of an earlier setup message no longer starts pairing again after it has succeeded. That second attempt could hide the newly connected device’s reports until the pairing window closed. @faronov makes a first contribution to zigpy with these corrections, after observing both problems with several relays in range.

articles.title: Close a group of blinds that is still slightly open
articles.dek: Both the position and tilt calculations preserve the close control when rounding would otherwise make the group look shut.
body: One blind left a fraction open could disappear in the group’s rounded-down average, producing a position of zero. Home Assistant then disabled the close action even though something remained open.
The group uses a minimum reported position of 1 while any member is open, and applies the same rule to tilt. Other averaged positions keep their existing rounding.
